goldens.comment: Unsafe raw List deserialization without type safety. Calling Optional.get() directly on the Optional returned by RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) without checking isPresent() can lead to a NoSuchElementException if the Optional is empty.

After creating the RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, consider setting its id from the stored credential (e.g., myUser.recoveryCodes.getId()); otherwise getId() will be null and downstream removal by id (e.g., removeStoredCredentialById in the authenticator flow) may not work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — validateCredential's recovery-code branch never removes/marks the matched code as used, so a leaked code can be replayed indefinitely for repeated logins (recovery codes should be single-use)

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...) the newly added RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE branch deserializes the stored List and returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` without updating/removing the matched code from `myUser.recoveryCodes` (or otherwise marking it used). This makes any valid recovery code indefinitely replayable for subsequent logins within this user-storage implementation, which violates the expected single-use semantics of recovery codes and can lead to incorrect/security-relevant behavior in tests using this provider.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:340 — No locking/CAS around the recovery-code check-then-use path, so two concurrent requests submitting the same code before either "consumes" it could both succeed (compounded by codes never being invalidated at all)

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)`, the new RecoveryAuthnCodes branch deserializes the stored list and returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))` without removing/consuming the matched code or updating stored credential data. That means the same recovery code can be reused indefinitely; consequently, concurrent submissions would also both succeed (the finding’s locking/CAS comment is less relevant because there is no consume step at all, but the ‘codes never being invalidated’ part is directly verifiable from the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:245 — getCredentials silently swallows IOException on recovery-codes JSON deserialization (log.error + continue), causing a corrupted/tampered credential to silently vanish from the user's credential list rather than surfacing/failing the operation

adjudication.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(...)`, the new recovery-codes branch catches `IOException` from `JsonSerialization.readValue(...)`, logs an error, and continues without adding the recovery-codes credential to the returned list. That does mean a malformed/corrupted recovery-codes JSON value will result in the credential not appearing in `getCredentials` output. However, the diff doesn’t show a contract requiring `getCredentials` to fail/throw on parse errors (and this is a testsuite/backwards-compat provider), so it’s more of a robustness/diagnostic/design concern than a clearly verifiable defect. Also, it’s not fully “silent” since it logs an error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:126 — createRecoveryCodesCredential uses user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...) purely as a support probe; if updateCredential has any side effect for federated storage that doesn't fully support the type, this could leave partially-written/inconsistent credential state that's hard to detect since only the boolean return is checked

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, the diff shows it always calls `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(recoveryCodesCredential)` first and only falls back to `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(...)` if the boolean return is false. There is no explicit capability check or rollback logic in this method, so the correctness of using `updateCredential` as the “try user storage first” decision point depends on federated implementations being side-effect-free when returning `false`. The diff itself doesn’t prove that partial writes can happen, but it does introduce this new pattern for recovery codes and relies solely on the boolean result.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:73 — Indentation/whitespace reformatting of an unrelated existing method (getConfigurableAuthenticatorFactory) is mixed into a feature diff, adding review noise unrelated to recovery-code support

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show only whitespace/indentation changes in `getConfigurableAuthenticatorFactory` (lines around `CredentialHelper.java:73`) with no behavioral change, mixed into the recovery-codes feature work. However, this is purely a style/formatting nit and the categories define such findings as "hallucination" (i.e., not a substantive review issue/defect).

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/CredentialHelper.java:120 — createRecoveryCodesCredential rethrows JsonSerialization IOException as unchecked RuntimeException, which will surface as an unhandled 500 in the required-action flow instead of a clean failureChallenge/error to the user

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)` which does `JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)` and on `IOException` throws a new unchecked `RuntimeException` (no handling at call sites). `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.processAction` now calls this helper and then proceeds to `reqActionContext.success()` without any try/catch or `failureChallenge`, so if serialization ever fails it will bubble up as a server error rather than a clean user-facing failure. However, since `generatedCodes` is a `List<String>`, Jackson serialization is expected to be reliably safe in normal operation, making this more of a robustness/UX concern than a concrete, likely defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/forms/login/freemarker/model/RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean.java:17 — Constructor calls credentialModelOpt.get() without isPresent() check; if credential is missing/deleted (race or storage failure) this throws NoSuchElementException with an unhelpful stack trace instead of a clear auth error

adjudication.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` constructor, the diff changes to `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` but then immediately calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` without checking presence. If the user has no recovery-codes credential (e.g., deleted or not configured), this will throw `NoSuchElementException` rather than producing a controlled/auth-friendly error path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/servers/auth-server/services/testsuite-providers/src/main/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.java:197 — Recovery codes are stored as plaintext JSON (input.getChallengeResponse()) instead of hashed, unlike the standard RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel which stores hashed codes

adjudication.rationale: In BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential(), the recovery codes credential is persisted as raw JSON via `recoveryCodesModel.setCredentialData(input.getChallengeResponse())`. The same plaintext JSON is later deserialized in `isValid()` and compared with `equals(input.getChallengeResponse())`, confirming the codes are stored and validated in plaintext rather than a hashed/one-way form. This is a verifiable security-sensitive behavior introduced by the diff for recovery codes support in this user storage provider.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/federation/storage/BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest.java:510 — testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin only exercises the happy path; no test covers reusing an already-consumed recovery code or submitting an invalid code

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new integration test `testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin` in `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorageTest` that configures a browser flow with `RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator`, sets up recovery codes via required action, and then logs in by entering a generated code (happy path only). The test never attempts a second login using the same already-entered code, nor does it attempt submitting an invalid/unknown recovery code. Given recovery codes are typically single-use and input validation is part of the new flow exercised here, the absence of negative/edge-case coverage is a concrete, diff-grounded gap in the newly added test coverage rather than a verified functional defect.
